item.title: Using GNU Stow for managing your dotfiles
item.author: me@example.com (John Doe)
item.description:
Using GNU Stow for managing your dotfiles

A few years back, I discovered a program called GNU Stow through a video on Wolfgang’s Channel which is as defined by the man page

"a symlink farm manager which takes distinct packages of software and/or data located in separate directories on the filesystem, and makes them appear to be installed in the same place."

I found that it was very useful for managing your dotfiles and various configurations in a clean manner instead of having to manually symlink everything together, and today I will guide you on how to use it so you can worry about configuring neovim instead of worrying about if everything is symlinked or not.
